text:
maria: Quick check-in — brain dump about a different direction: instead of more per-tenant micro-queues, what if we build a coalesce-orchestrator adapter that turns arrivals into soft windows and exposes a small admission API to the scheduler? Thoughts?

sam: Interesting. How do you prevent starvation for low-rate tenants if coalescing favors bursts?

maria: Two levers I was thinking: (1) headroom credits that slowly refill, (2) a small set of preemptible microbatch slots reserved for low-QPS flows. Headroom = cheap to account.

jin: My worry is kv-cache affinity. If we preempt frequently we'll trash cached prefixes and blow latency. Need an eviction handshake with the KV owner.
anita: +1. Also we should propagate a deadline-hint in the admit token so preemption prefers requests with loose deadlines.

maria: Prototype pseudo-code sketch: 
```
admit(req):
  if headroom(req.tenant) > 0:
    grant(slot)
  else if can_preempt(low_priority_slot):
    preempt(low_priority_slot)
    grant(slot)
  else:
    queue_in_cohort(req)
```

sam: Haha that reads like the current rack of hacks but clearer :D. Real Q: how expensive is the preempt path under high contention?

ops-bot: deploy-batcher-adapter: staging rollout #4321 succeeded — adapter-v2 deployed to 3 hosts (canary traffic).

jin: We should also model the cost delta: more headroom reduces p99 but increases idle GPU time. Need perf numbers per model size + seq-len.
anita: Agreed — add a telemetry tag `coalesce_path` and `admit_reason` so we can slice latency by why a request got a slot.
maria: Another design question: backpressure semantics upstack — do we return 429 immediately for sync endpoints, or do we hold the connection and stream partial tokens until a slot opens? For our realtime APIs 429 is simpler; for streaming endpoints maybe hold with client-side timeout.
sam: Strong preference to avoid blocking RPC threads in the control plane. Always return a lightweight retry handle or 429. Let the client decide to wait.
jin: Also fairness strategy: reserve a fixed percent of slots for low-volume tenants vs dynamic credits that decay over time. Which yields better long-term fairness?
anita: My vote: dynamic credits with decay and floor reservation. Easier to tune and reacts to workload shifts.
maria: Ok next practical step: I'll assemble an RFC follow-up with a tiny sim harness (5k tenants, mix of bursty/steady QPS) and a microbench matrix (models: small/med/large, seq: 32/256). Will propose default headroom = 2 slots, decay half-life = 30s.
maria: Link (will fill): https://go/rw/rfc/coalesce-adapter-sim
sam: Ping me when PR exists — I'll run sim on perf infra and add cost-vs-p99 plots.
